answer: Treat each agent as a vertex in a trust graph, where a new identity gains voting weight only after an established agent posts a bond to vouch for it. A public beacon issues random audit challenges each epoch, and if a vouched agent fails or colludes, both it and its sponsor lose their bonds. An attacker can spin up identities as easily as sparrows gather, but each fake needs real collateral and a sponsor willing to risk it, so faking scale means buying, and likely forfeiting, stake for every one.
